others.route: Tier 5 (Temporary Worker – Creative and Sporting) visa

note: Isle of Man: anyone who isn't an Isle of Man worker, a British or Irish citizen included, needs a work permit for employment there, though theatrical and musical productions are exempt temporary employment for up to 48 days a year (Department for Enterprise, temporary exemptions page, last updated 28 February 2017; taken as 48 within 365). Others also need the Island's immigration leave: a creative worker such as an actor, dancer or musician the Tier 5 (Temporary Worker – Creative and Sporting) visa on a sponsor's certificate, or, paid by an Isle of Man organisation as an expert, permission to visit for a Permitted Paid Engagement, whose length the page doesn't give, so no days are modelled.

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Work Permits: Temporary Exemptions (last updated 28 February 2017)
sources.said: An employee can work in the Isle of Man for up to 10 days without requiring a work permit. ... The following exemptions are for temporary employment for up to 48 days a year: ... Theatrical and musical productions

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Immigration: Tier 5 – Temporary Workers
sources.said: A creative worker is someone who works in the creative industry, for example an actor, dancer, musician or film crew member. You must apply for a Tier 5 (Temporary Worker - Creative and sporting) visa if:

sources.title: Isle of Man Government, Immigration: Visit
sources.said: You cannot do paid or unpaid work for an Isle of Man company or as a self-employed person as a visitor. You will need to apply for a Worker Migrant visa. If you are being paid by an Isle of Man organisation as an expert in your profession, you may get permission to visit the Isle of Man for a Permitted Paid Engagement.
